newsitem.title: BELGIUM: French-paid mercenaries in Zaire, opposition says.
newsitem.headline: French-paid mercenaries in Zaire, opposition says.

text.p: A leading Zairean opposition party said on Thursday that some 300 mercenaries paid by France were in Zaire to support Zairean president Mobutu's regime and another 700 had been recruited.

"There are at least 300 mercenaries in Zaire, another 700 have been recruited and are spread over different locations elsewhere," Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) spokeswoman Justine M'Poyo Kasa-Vubu told a news conference.
"Paris has accepted to support this action...the French are paying for it," she said.

She said the mercenaries were from France, Belgium and South Africa. She added that, politically, France could no longer afford to send its own troops to Zaire and was therefore helping Mobutu establish a mercenary force.

Paris daily Le Monde said on Tuesday that a force of South African, French, Belgian, British, Angolan and Mozambican mercenaries had gathered in eastern Zaire. It said the force numbered between 200 and 300 but was expected to grow rapidly.
The mercenaries are needed both to help Mobutu crush Laurent Kabila's rebel army in eastern Zaire as well as to help Mobutu keep his position, Kasa-Vubu said.
Kasa-Vubu -- daughter of Zaire's first president Joseph Kasa-Vubu, who was overthrown by Mobutu -- said that France wants to play a role in Mobutu's succession.
Mobutu returned to France on Thursday to consult doctors about his health. He flew back to Zaire on December 17 after four months in Switzerland and France for cancer surgery.
"France wants a successor who will be as amenable (to French interests) as Mobutu," Kasa-Vubu said.
She suggested that General Mahele, Zaire's new army chief, could be a French choice. "If General Mahele does not distance himself from the French, he will be condemned by popular anger," she said.
Mobutu appointed Mahele as army chief in mid-December. His main mission is to crush Kabila's rebel army.
Kasa-Vubu stopped short of supporting Kabila but said "He is Zairean and he has the same goals as us: a return the rule of law and the eradication of dictatorship."
"Kabila has taken to violence, it is the only language Mobutu understands," she said.
She said the UDPS was preparing to abandon its non-violent stance. "We want to move towards legitimate defensive action," she said, but refused to go into detail.
During his 31-year rule Mobutu has on several occasions employed mercenaries and foreign troops to put down rebellions.
